Version: 0.2 · 2026-09-09 · Direction accepted by Rex; evidence and detailed checks continue to evolve.
Owner: Rex. Canonical home: this Notion page. The repository's IDEAL_STATE.md points here.
Rex endorses the document and refines the central promise to make no additional team members an explicit constraint. This accepts the direction, not a claim that its outcomes are achieved. Population, observation periods and numerical success thresholds remain to be defined.
Intent, in Rex's words

“i think it's a missing piecce in helping guide the work we do together and i like the idea of crafting and refining an ideal state artifact for each project. Attain Prep will be the first to use this approach for me.”
The desired experience

Central promise: Students make independent, measurable progress toward their SAT goal, using the time they can realistically give. Parents understand that progress and know when their support would help. Rex can run a useful, sustainable product without personally directing every family's preparation or hiring additional team members.

From the student's perspective: “I know what to work on and why. It fits the time I have. If I get stuck, I can get useful teaching and then try for myself. I can stop and return without losing my place. I can see what I am getting better at and what still needs work.”
From the parent's perspective: “I can tell whether preparation is helping, what remains uncertain, and whether there is something useful for me to do.”
The product should feel like one continuous preparation journey. The exact set of pages, activity names, tutor model and tutorial format can change while these outcomes remain the aim.
How this uses Miessler's idea

His articulation article proposes a living artifact that states the desired outcome, makes implicit expectations explicit, and connects claims to verification. We adopt that direction here: intent, current evidence, criteria and revisions have one home. Detailed technical documents support it and link back; they do not independently redefine success.

The ARC article illustrates recording a belief, choosing an experiment that could refute it, and retaining the result even when the belief was wrong. Its reported benchmark performance does not establish effectiveness for this education product.

The Deutsch conversation explores making success criteria explicit while refining subjective preferences through human feedback. For this project, “feels coherent” needs student observation and Rex's judgment as well as software checks. A passing test cannot establish that a student learned or understood the experience.
This is our adaptation, not an installation of PAI or a claim to implement Miessler's full system.
Criteria and current evidence

These criteria give the accepted direction stable IDs and a next check. Their detailed checks can be refined as evidence improves. Product-wide attainment is unverified until the relevant population, observation period and decision threshold are agreed. An individual successful observation only verifies that case. No overall completion percentage is calculated.
IS-01 · Learning lasts beyond the helped question

Desired state: After teaching, a student can apply the concept independently to a fresh question on a later occasion.
Check: Record the teaching exposure, a fresh independent check, and a later fresh check. Show successes and attempts, concept and elapsed interval. Assisted responses cannot pass an independent check. Repeated delayed failure challenges the teaching approach.
Current evidence: The approved tutor direction calls for this. The percentage walkthrough is a proposal. Neither proves current learning gains.
Next gap: Make the learning evidence testable in the tutor pilot. Sources: docs/tutor-direction.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-tutor-walkthrough-design.md.
IS-02 · A student can begin without a guide beside them

Desired state: A new student can choose and start useful practice without help navigating the app.
Check: Observe a new student from login to the first learning action without coaching. Record where help or guessing was needed. Ask why they chose that action afterward.
Current evidence: First-session confusion is reported in FB-002. Guidance and the progressive tutorial shipped; post-release student comprehension remains unverified.
Next gap: Observe a real first session and the parent-to-student handoff. A shipped tooltip alone does not close this criterion.
IS-03 · Practice fits the student's available time

Desired state: The student can stop when their available time ends and later continue from clearly saved progress.
Check: Start with a declared short time budget, stop partway through an activity, leave and return. Verify the saved answers and next action, and ask whether stopping felt legitimate. In an assessment, explain the effect of pausing on the interpretation of timing/results.
Current evidence: FB-009 supports flexible time as valued. FB-010 reports a 40-question commitment without an obvious exit; existing persistence does not prove a usable pause journey.
Next gap: Investigate the complete skill-check stop/resume experience before choosing a redesign.
IS-04 · Each learning activity has a clear purpose and continuation

Desired state: After an activity, a student can identify the useful next step and how it relates to the work just completed.
Check: Walk through a skill gap, practice, a mistake, help/review and return to the daily plan. Ask the student what each transition is for. A dead end or unexplained detour challenges the journey.
Current evidence: FB-011 describes useful concepts that feel buried and disconnected. A-002 and the tutorial proposal provide a partial journey map.
Next gap: Use that map to investigate transitions and discovery across Today, Progress, skill checks, tutoring and review.
IS-05 · Challenge follows evidence about this learner

Desired state: The next practice challenge is justified by evidence about the student's current needs.
Check: Compare learners with different recent independent results in the same skill. Inspect what is selected and why. Test the rationale against later performance; a difficulty label alone cannot establish suitability.
Current evidence: FB-012 records authored easy/medium/hard labels and no learner-adaptive drill difficulty in the inspected implementation. Labels are not calibrated SAT module routes.
Next gap: Investigate question coverage, selection and calibration before promising adaptive difficulty or equivalent SAT routing.
IS-06 · Progress claims match the evidence

Desired state: Every displayed claim about readiness or improvement is supported by evidence appropriate to that claim.
Check: Trace selected claims back to the attempts or test results that support them. Probe sparse data, assisted answers, repeated exposed questions and stale observations. Record unknowns explicitly.
Current evidence: FB-005 values content-gap and timing reports. FB-007 accepts missing predictions with too few attempts. That supports preserving honest uncertainty; it does not validate predictive accuracy.
Next gap: Inspect the evidence behind timing, mastery and score displays as those areas change. Keep speed practice distinguishable from learning with help.
IS-07 · Parents can use the report to make a useful decision

Desired state: A parent can identify an appropriate next action, including choosing to give the student space, from the reported evidence.
Check: Give a parent the normal report without explanation. Ask what it tells them and what they would do. Compare their interpretation with the supporting records.
Current evidence: Atanas values the reports, but we have not established which decisions they improve. Brian relays positive first-session feedback.
Next gap: Ask about a concrete decision in a follow-up interview. Minutes, streaks and tutor usage remain activity measures.
IS-08 · Families can maintain access without losing learning history

Desired state: A family can correct a student's sign-in address while retaining the same student and learning record.
Check: Use a test family to correct the address, sign in again and verify record continuity. Check that another family cannot make the change.
Current evidence: FB-001 documents the wrong-email problem; the implementation brief remains P1 and unshipped in the feedback log.
Next gap: Execute the existing email-correction brief within the normal release process. This draft does not reorder that priority.
IS-09 · The product supports a sustainable business

Desired state: Attain Prep delivers continuing learning value and supports a sustainable business operated by Rex alone, augmented by AI, without hiring additional team members. Its service costs and Rex's workload stay within limits he accepts.
Check: For a defined cohort and period, examine continued use, payment/renewal, AI and infrastructure costs, and Rex's actual operating time. Include support, content quality checks, product development, billing issues, incident recovery, and supervising or repairing AI work. Track recurring manual interventions as family numbers change. Agree workload and cost thresholds before declaring success.
What would count against feasibility: quality, service or learning outcomes deteriorate unless Rex adds team members or sustains more operating time than he is willing to give. Routine AI output that requires substantial human correction is operating work, not eliminated work.
Current evidence: Rex explicitly states this is a test of a one-man operation augmented by AI and that he does not want to hire additional team members. Solo feasibility, retention, economics and acceptable workload are not yet demonstrated. Historical experiment pricing is not adopted as today's price.
Next gap: Establish Rex's operating-time baseline and acceptable limit alongside a target customer scale. Learning value, commercial viability and solo operating feasibility each need evidence.
Boundaries that shape success

Preserve family data separation, learning records and honest billing/access behavior. Help must not silently become independent assessment evidence. Easy signup, flexible practice time and useful reporting are existing positives to preserve.

Do not treat more questions, more tutor chat, longer screen time, a streak, or a shipped feature as proof of learning. Do not promise a particular SAT increase without supporting evidence. The original family deployment and market product remain distinct scopes.

The tutor is a proposed means to better learning. Whether it eventually directs the entire daily journey is still open. The current tutorial and 40-question skill-check format are also means that can change.

Operating constraint, confirmed by Rex: one human operator, augmented by AI, with no additional team members. Plans must fit that model. If a proposal depends on adding staff, revise the scope or operating approach and make the conflict explicit. Growth alone is not success if it breaks the operating constraint.
How this guides our work

Working rule: Before starting product work, name the relevant IS criterion, the observed gap and the evidence the work should produce. Include the expected ongoing work for Rex and what AI or the product will handle, where the change affects operations. Small changes need only a short reference, not another specification. This operational assessment follows Rex's explicit solo-business constraint.
Use the existing flow: feedback provides evidence → this artifact explains why the gap matters → a queue task defines the next useful step → the result updates our evidence here.

For each queue brief, include the Ideal State page/version, relevant criterion IDs, current gap, proposed change or investigation, what would count against the hypothesis, and the outcome check in Done when. A task outside existing criteria should explain the missing outcome; extend the artifact deliberately instead of forcing a weak match.

At completion, report separately: implementation/release status, verification evidence, and whether the desired student or parent outcome was observed. Include the date, app version or commit, cohort/conditions and limits where relevant. Failed checks remain visible and inform the next attempt.

Rex owns changes to the central promise, trade-offs and outcome thresholds. Agents can draft refinements and record evidence. Keep a dated reason for criterion changes; do not weaken a criterion to make completed work look successful.

Current integration: This artifact is linked from the feedback hub and repository. The queue runner does not automatically load this page. Its automation is unchanged. The queue still starts only when a task is set to Ready; endorsing or refining this artifact does not launch product work. Automatic loading remains a separate integration step.
Refinement decisions

Resolved September 9, 2026: Rex endorses the Ideal State document and refines the central promise to exclude hiring additional team members. Attain Prep is explicitly a test of whether a one-person business augmented by AI is feasible. The independent-progress promise remains the working direction.

Then define the intended learner range and preparation horizon, what evidence would make Rex trust the learning claim, and the business scale and owner workload he wants. Current family feedback includes both short daily sessions far from the SAT and a student near test day; one family's horizon should not silently define everyone.
Revision record

2026-09-09, v0.1: Rex requests the Ideal State approach for Attain Prep as the first project. Initial articulation assembled from his feedback, the agreed tutor direction, existing strategy documents and the three linked Miessler articles. Product criteria and workflow integration are drafted for refinement. No criteria are declared achieved. No product tasks or deployments are started by this document.

2026-09-09, v0.2: Rex endorses the document after directly adding ‘or hiring additional team members’ to the central promise. His clarification: ‘i have no desire to hire additional team members. this is a test of whether or not running something like this is feasible with a one-man operation augmented by AI.’ Preserved his edit and carried the constraint into IS-09, operating boundaries and work selection. Evidence checks now include the human effort to supervise and repair AI work. No workload limit or business scale is invented, and feasibility remains unverified.

Version 0.2 · 9 September 2026 · Owner: Rex

Status: working draft for refinement. Rex has confirmed the one-human operating constraint and the ambition to achieve first-page search visibility and leading AI-result visibility relative to competitors. The proposed positioning, detailed measurement definitions and numerical success thresholds still need refinement. Desired outcomes are not claims of attainment.
Central promise

People planning a move, a visit, or life in Portugal know what to do next and why. They can rely on clear, current, independent guidance that helps them make sound decisions. Ultimate Portugal becomes a leading independent English-language Portugal resource: its relevant pages earn first-page search positions and prominent citations or recommendations in AI answers for the reader questions we choose to own.
Ultimate Portugal earns sustainable affiliate income while running with one human operator supported by AI, with very little routine intervention and occasional specialist help when needed.
Rex's intent, preserved

my ultimate goal is to get to a place that this entire operation runs autonomously with very little human interaction. but that means we have a MECE view of everything necessary to deliver Ultimate Portugal
Yes, use the same constraint, I'll allow occasional paid specialist if needed - but ideally we're talking a one human operator supported by AI.

it's looking pretty decent - but we don't have anything in there as it relates to positioning in the marketplace vs. other competitors. i'd like it to be a front-page ranking, top-AI results ranking page ideally

The target is a viable one-person operation. AI supervision, corrections, troubleshooting, approvals, account administration and managing specialists all count as human work. Moving hidden labor to a contractor or another inbox does not satisfy the constraint. An occasional specialist can resolve a bounded knowledge or judgment need; routine delivery must not depend on hiring a standing team. This allowance does not approve a specific purchase or engagement.
Whose outcomes matter
Readers: understand their options, limits and next step; can find relevant information and judge its reliability without sorting through conflicting or stale advice.
Subscribers and correspondents: receive what the site promises, retain control over email and data, and receive appropriate handling of questions or corrections.
Rex: owns a useful, financially sustainable site whose routine work completes within standing rules. He can see real outcomes and unresolved decisions without supervising each job.
Partners and listed businesses: are represented accurately and evaluated on editorial merit. Affiliate income does not buy a recommendation or a directory place.
Confirmed direction and boundaries
One human operator supported by AI, with occasional specialist input if needed.
Comprehensive ownership of necessary business outcomes, including capabilities that are missing today.
Existing business scope: English-language guidance for moving to, visiting and living in Portugal; associated tools, directory and the promised weekly reader newsletter.
Existing monetization scope: affiliate income. Ads, paid listings, lead generation and newsletter sponsorship are outside the current mandate.
Editorial trust: no invented first-hand experience, credentials, sources, observations or results. Explain material uncertainty and ground consequential claims in appropriate evidence.
Consent remains purpose-specific. A contact or listing application does not give newsletter consent.
Existing publishing, topic blessing, external messaging, spending and release permissions remain in force. Any later reduction in routine approval must come from an explicit standing policy.

The topical map serves useful coverage and a defensible market position. Competitive search and AI visibility are explicit desired outcomes alongside reader value, trust, net economics and low owner workload. Article volume, traffic or a single ranking win cannot establish the whole Ideal State.
Market position and competitive ambition

Confirmed ambition: Ultimate Portugal should be a first-page search result and a prominent source or recommendation in leading AI answers for the Portugal topics that matter to its readers. This applies across relevant pages and selected reader journeys; it is not limited to ranking the homepage or the brand name.

Proposed positioning: the independent, practical Portugal decision resource that connects moving, visiting and living in one coherent journey. Its reason to be chosen is source-grounded, date-checked guidance, original useful evidence, maintained comparison tools and editorially vetted services that make the next action clear. AI-supported production is the operating method, not the reader-facing reason to trust us.

Test that positioning against actual competing answers. A page should contribute a useful advantage the reader can name: clearer tradeoffs, better-supported or fresher facts, relevant original analysis, an actionable comparison, or a more complete next step. Do not claim that rivals lack these qualities without current evidence.

Use the existing 12-site competitor research as the starting peer set, grouped by reader task. Relocation and practical-life examples: Portugalist, Expatica Portugal, Anchorless, Nomad Gate and Global Citizen Solutions. Travel examples: Portugal.com, Earth Trekkers, Salt in Our Hair, A Dangerous Business and Julie Dawn Fox. Specialist examples include iSchoolAdvisor and Practice Portuguese. These are research peers, not a claimed current ranking order. Add newly observed competitors and official sources when they appear in the same results; distinguish publishers from government authorities rather than excluding strong results.

Define the contest before scoring it: a versioned set of important non-branded queries and natural-language questions mapped to topical tasks; named countries, language, devices and AI surfaces; a comparison cohort; an observation period; and a deadline. US and UK English are a proposed starting scope because existing keyword evidence covers them, with much greater depth in the US. Keep visitor, mover and resident topic results visible separately. Missing pages and hard queries stay visible; do not select only easy wins or change the basket without a revision record.

Report observed top-10 and top-3 organic coverage, competitor coverage differences, AI citation rate, explicit recommendation rate, response prominence where meaningful, and each metric’s measured sample and missing observations. Use the same queries, settings and period for competitors. Separate branded demand from non-branded discovery. Paid placements do not count as organic ranking wins. Better visibility must still bring relevant readers, useful answers and a viable business.

Evidence today: the 9 September DataForSEO research validates demand and competitor coverage, not Ultimate Portugal’s current leadership. The 12-question, five-engine visibility benchmark is implemented but the audited store contains no actual answer-engine observations. No current first-page coverage rate, AI leadership rate or competitor superiority is asserted. Source anchors: docs/research/topical-map-2026-09-09/README.md and engine/visibility/benchmark.json.
Ideal State criteria and current evidence

There are fifteen criteria. None is declared achieved. Rex has confirmed the direction of competitive search and AI visibility; the detailed formulations and acceptance thresholds below remain proposed. UP-ISC-07 applies only if optional channels are selected. The 52 capabilities map exactly once to a primary criterion; shared dependencies do not duplicate ownership. Observation windows, samples and thresholds still need agreement. There is no overall percentage complete.
UP-ISC-01 · The business fits one human operator
Desired state: Routine operation fits Rex's agreed time budget without depending on an ongoing team.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.

Current evidence: Confirmed owner intent: one human supported by AI, occasional paid specialists if needed. Selected controls exist. Total owner time, interruption load, capacity and long-term solo feasibility are not measured. External account and privacy setup remain unverified.

Check the system: Run allowed and denied action fixtures for publication, paid calls, personal-data handling, and credential use. Check a current promise, decision, budget, access, vendor, and renewal register.

Check the actual experience: Owner confirms that normal weekly work fits the agreed time limit and that exceptions reach them with a decision-ready record. Owner reviews a sampled privacy request and account-recovery drill.

What would count against the claim: Routine delivery requires a standing team or exceeds Rex's agreed time budget across the agreed observation period. AI supervision, repair work or repeated specialist reliance is excluded from the reported workload.
Next gap: No verified end-to-end rights request or account recovery; No operation-wide cost reservation and exhaustion control; No single capacity plan or service-promise register.
Threshold or scope to agree: Needs owner decision: maximum owner minutes per week, monthly operating budget, and acceptable exception load.
Primary capability IDs: mandate, authority, spending, privacy, capacity, security, continuity.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-12.
UP-ISC-02 · Readers can trust the evidence
Desired state: Every material public claim and reusable content asset has dated, suitable evidence and rights that can be traced when it changes or is challenged.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.

Current evidence: Partial. Source collection, protected refresh facts and rent checks exist. As of 10 September 2026, the search-evidence repair is merged as 574490f. Automatic A6/A7 shared-input assembly and hash checks pass offline tests on reviewed branch claude/refresh-input-guard (09e2f8f), awaiting merge. This proves input consistency, not factual quality. Several source adapters, a claim dependency register, an original-evidence plan and an asset-rights register remain missing. Execution evidence is in the Content machine closure queue.

Check the system: Sample claims, calculator inputs, images, and sourced passages for source, date, rights, expiry, and affected-page links. Simulate an authoritative fact change and confirm that dependent pages and tools enter review.
Check the actual experience: Editor or owner judges whether source quality and any original reporting support the reader-facing assertion. Rights owner confirms permissions for a sampled asset.
What would count against the claim: A published material claim cannot be sourced, dated, updated, or corrected An asset enters a release without known permitted use
Next gap: Unconfigured source adapters; No full claim-to-output impact map; No asset provenance ledger.
Threshold or scope to agree: Unset: define material-claim risk classes and review deadlines.
Primary capability IDs: sources, claims, original, datasets, rights.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-01, UP-ISC-12.
UP-ISC-03 · Readers know what to do next
Desired state: A reader can identify a useful next step from an article or tool and explain why it fits their situation.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.

Current evidence: Partial. Draft checks, editorial contracts, citations and affiliate-link checks exist. The inactive v2 new-article contract and recoverable evidence tools merged as 4e45ea1; their runtime fixture is synthetic. The scheduled new-article route still uses the existing retired-guidance contract. Readiness remains 0/3 qualifying clean refreshes, followed by a real shadow article, coordinated activation and observed morning outcomes. Independent real v2 article quality remains unproven.
Check the system: Run source, claim, citation, affiliate-link, metadata, asset, and internal-link checks against a bundle. Verify that a changed bundle component invalidates prior approval.

Check the actual experience: Ask representative readers to use an article/tool for a realistic move, visit or living-in-Portugal task without coaching; record their next action, rationale and any material misunderstanding. An independent source-grounded review checks whether their interpretation is justified; a completed user journey does not override factual concerns.
What would count against the claim: A release passes mechanical checks yet misleads, omits needed context, or fails its stated reader task
Next gap: No single bound bundle manifest; No consistent current writer and voice route; No reader-task validation.
Threshold or scope to agree: Needs decision: define the sampled reader-task pass rate and the material-error bar.
Primary capability IDs: drafting, voice-policy, article-qa, visuals, packaging.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-02, UP-ISC-08.
UP-ISC-04 · Authorized changes complete reliably
Desired state: An approved public change reaches the intended live version once, and a failed or duplicated job can recover without a duplicate side effect.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.
Current evidence: Partial: approved publishing paths, preview tools, deploy checks, cron, and locks exist. Signed decision dispatch, cross-workflow idempotency, and restore drills are unverified.

Check the system: Exercise approval expiry, duplicate delivery, failed deploy, late event, retry exhaustion, rollback, and isolated restore fixtures. Check the public version and the relevant SSR routes after a controlled release.
Check the actual experience: Owner confirms the approved artifact and result record match their decision. Owner observes a restore drill with no duplicate mail, publication, or paid action.
What would count against the claim: One decision causes two external effects A failed job silently disappears The prior good state cannot be restored safely
Next gap: No proven dead-letter and reconciliation path; No verified external-state restoration; No complete approval-expiry service level.
Threshold or scope to agree: Unset: owner must choose recovery-time and acceptable-data-loss limits.
Primary capability IDs: approval, release, deployment, orchestration, recovery.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-01, UP-ISC-03, UP-ISC-12.
UP-ISC-05 · Known errors and stale facts are resolved
Desired state: Known material errors and overdue facts are resolved within agreed risk-based deadlines, with affected outputs and notices handled.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.
Current evidence: Partial: refresh, correction records, and diagnosis for consolidate/redirect/prune exist. Recent refresh attempts failed and full lifecycle execution is not proven.
Check the system: Create stale, corrected, and consolidation fixtures; verify queueing, affected-page updates, redirects, links, map, and sitemap.
Check the actual experience: Owner judges error severity and any needed reader notice. Sample readers confirm that a correction or redirect leaves them with a usable answer.
What would count against the claim: A known high-risk claim remains live past its deadline A retirement breaks useful intent or leaves outdated discovery paths
Next gap: No all-content risk-based freshness coverage; No tested urgent correction-to-notice path; No complete retirement reconciliation.
Threshold or scope to agree: Needs decision: severity deadlines and maximum overdue high-risk pages.
Primary capability IDs: refresh, corrections, retirement.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-02, UP-ISC-04, UP-ISC-09.
UP-ISC-06 · Readers can find and use the answer
Desired state: A reader can find and use eligible public information through site navigation or search on the devices and assistive methods that matter.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.
Current evidence: Partial: catalog, search, topics, feeds, machine-readable twins, and SEO shadow execution are implemented. Recurring index and accessibility outcome evidence is incomplete.
Check the system: Check catalog, feeds, canonicals, robots, sitemap, structured data, index signals, broken links, keyboard paths, responsive layouts, and performance budgets.

Check the actual experience: Representative readers find a selected answer from search and complete article, search, comparison, tool, and form journeys. Assistive-technology users or a qualified specialist sample the critical journeys.
What would count against the claim: Eligible content is missing or materially broken in a promised discovery surface A critical reader task fails on a representative device or keyboard journey
Next gap: No proven indexing-loss incident loop; No recurring assistive-technology validation; Shadow SEO is not reader-discovery proof.
Threshold or scope to agree: Needs decision: priority journeys, device set, and acceptable discovery failure rate.
Primary capability IDs: findability, technical-search, experience-health.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-04, UP-ISC-05, UP-ISC-12.
UP-ISC-07 · Optional channels earn their place
Desired state: Any chosen optional growth channel earns relevant attention within its agreed cost and owner-time limits.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: conditional: only if the owner chooses extra channels.
Current evidence: Missing: RSS and JSON feeds exist, but no repeatable earned-reference or selected-channel operating loop is established.
Check the system: Check each active channel and outreach record for audience, owner, cadence, permitted account, cost, measurement, and stop rule.
Check the actual experience: Owner reviews sampled outreach and references for relevance and editorial fit. Reader feedback identifies whether the channel brought the expected audience.
What would count against the claim: Work becomes link spam, attracts the wrong audience, or continues after its stop rule
Next gap: No approved external-channel portfolio; No qualified-reference or reader-fit evidence.
Threshold or scope to agree: Unset: select channels only after the owner sets a time and cost cap.
Primary capability IDs: authority-growth, channels.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-01, UP-ISC-02, UP-ISC-06.
UP-ISC-08 · Work follows real reader needs
Desired state: Work is selected from evidenced reader needs and strategic gaps, with bounded capacity rather than publishing volume as the goal.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.
Current evidence: Partial: a topical map, blessed backlog, and dated competitor research exist. No recurring reader-need synthesis or shared allocation plan exists.

Check the system: Check that proposals map to a topic, evidence source, owner decision, duplication check, and capacity allocation. Detect stale competitor inputs and repeated unresolved reader questions.

Check the actual experience: Owner reviews tradeoffs among news, evergreen work, refreshes, revenue work, and reader promises. Reader research validates ambiguous needs before they become investment decisions.
What would count against the claim: Duplicate or low-evidence work displaces an overdue reader need The queue grows without a declared tradeoff or stop condition
Next gap: No consent-aware theme synthesis; No recurring competitor change detection; No outcome-led prioritization across queues.
Threshold or scope to agree: Needs decision: queue age, freshness, and strategic-balance limits.
Primary capability IDs: portfolio, reader-demand.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-01, UP-ISC-09, UP-ISC-11.
UP-ISC-09 · Reader service promises are kept
Desired state: Readers receive the services the site promises, with their consent and control preserved.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.

Current evidence: Unverified or partial: consent separation and form intake exist, but production reader sends, sender health, suppression propagation, support closure, and directory review ledgers are not proven.
Check the system: Use controlled accounts to test signup, unsubscribe, suppression, validation, issue selection, rendering, delivery events, inquiry routing, and listing review dates.

Check the actual experience: Controlled inboxes confirm delivery and unsubscribe behavior. Readers assess the newsletter's usefulness and support closure; owner judges disputed listings and sensitive replies.
What would count against the claim: A non-consenting person is marketed to A subscribed reader cannot reliably stop mail An inaccurate or paid-influenced listing remains recommended
Next gap: No verified reader newsletter flow; No bounce/complaint and delivery evidence; No full support and directory decision trail.
Threshold or scope to agree: Needs decision: newsletter cadence tolerance, support-response deadline, and listing-review cadence.
Primary capability IDs: subscribe, reader-newsletter, email-health, support, directory.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-01, UP-ISC-04, UP-ISC-05.
UP-ISC-10 · The business earns sustainable affiliate income
Desired state: Useful, independent affiliate recommendations generate sustainable net contribution for the one-person business.
Status: proposed criterion; outcome-level attainment not established. Applies: core.

Current evidence: Missing to partial: the partner registry and link checks exist, but all registry programs show none; conversions, reversals, cash reconciliation, and reader-value conversion tests are not established.
Check the system: Test partner status, tracking redirect, disclosure, relation attributes, unavailable-offer detection, click accounting, and payout reconciliation fixtures.

Check the actual experience: Owner reviews partner terms, applications, payouts, and any commercial experiment before commitment. Readers or independent editorial review assess recommendation usefulness and disclosure clarity.

What would count against the claim: Recurring costs or owner effort exceed the agreed sustainable limits for the observation period. A recommendation follows commission rather than reader merit. Cash receipt is claimed without evidence, accrued commission is confused with cash, or unavailable conversion data is treated as zero.
Next gap: No active verified program and attributable conversion path; No commission-to-cash ledger; No trust-guarded recommendation experiments.
Threshold or scope to agree: Needs decision: minimum net contribution and reader-trust guardrails before scaling a partner.
Primary capability IDs: partners, commercial-links, attribution, cash, conversion.
Related criteria: UP-ISC-01, UP-ISC-03, UP-ISC-09, UP-ISC-11.
UP-ISC-11 · Decisions improve from honest evidence

How this artifact guides work

The Ideal State defines the outcomes. The topical map owns reader problems and content scope. The operating map identifies capabilities, gaps and dependencies. Feedback and measurements provide evidence. Selected work changes the system and returns evidence to this artifact.
Before starting a work item, record:
The primary Ideal State criterion and relevant capability IDs.
The observed gap, with dated evidence and what remains unknown.
The smallest intervention or experiment likely to improve that outcome.
What would show improvement, what would disprove the assumption, and any observation window.
The expected one-time and recurring human effort, AI/vendor cost, and required authority.
The stop or rollback condition, plus evidence to return when done.

Completion has two separate meanings: the change is implemented and checked; the intended outcome has been observed. A deployment may complete the first without establishing the second. Investigations can succeed by ruling out a proposed feature.

This is a proposed working rule. No automatic loading, queue trigger, dashboard refresh or execution permission was installed by creating the page. Existing approved priorities, including the new-article upgrade, remain intact while we connect them to outcomes.
Evidence and revision rules
Every criterion has a stable ID, a claim, a verification approach, current evidence and a next check.
Keep criterion approval status separate from evidence status. A proposed criterion is not an owner decision; a well-tested script is not proof of reader or business success.
Use not measured, partial evidence, supported within scope, or contradicted. Record the sample, period and limits. Missing evidence is not a failed result.
Separate current-state observations from desired conditions. Do not mark broad claims verified because their underlying workflows are green.
Retain failed probes and conflicting observations. Reopen a supported claim when new evidence contradicts it or its evidence expires.
Set thresholds before judging outcomes. Where Rex has not set a target, record that decision as open. Do not manufacture revenue, workload or quality targets.
Read-only checks may gather evidence within existing authority. A probe that spends money, contacts people, changes accounts or publishes requires the relevant standing authorization.
Refine this artifact when owner intent changes, evidence challenges a belief, or a selected work item produces a meaningful result. Preserve version history and the reason for changes.
Open decisions to refine
What counts as “very little” routine work: an acceptable weekly time budget, an interruption limit, and any absence period the operation must support.
What sustainable means financially: recurring cost ceiling, contribution or cash target, and the time horizon for reaching it.
Which reader group and high-value journeys lead the next phase when visitor and mover needs compete.
Which routine actions can eventually run under standing approval, and what quality evidence is required before that permission expands.
Which reader-outcome and freshness thresholds are meaningful for each risk level, rather than one universal standard.

Competitive ambition: which priority query/question basket, peer cohort, countries, devices and AI surfaces define the contest; what coverage and relative position count as success; and by when? First-page and leading-AI visibility are desired outcomes, not unmeasured accomplishments.
These detailed targets remain open in v0.2. The one-human constraint and the ambition for first-page search visibility and leading AI-result visibility are confirmed.
Known tensions to manage
More content can increase both coverage and the maintenance burden. Expand only when evidence, upkeep and usefulness can keep pace.
Revenue can conflict with impartial recommendations. Editorial merit remains the deciding rule.
Fewer approvals can reduce owner effort while increasing unnoticed-error risk. Use bounded authority, independent checks and tested recovery.
Original evidence can need real human input. Choose methods that deliver distinctive value within the one-person constraint; use occasional specialists only where needed.
A system can run unattended while delivering little value. Judge autonomy alongside reader outcomes, trust and net economics.
Starting point and next learning steps

The dated operating model contains 52 capabilities across 10 functions, including two optional growth methods. Its 50 core capabilities comprise six covered, 31 partial, seven with no repeatable implementation identified, and six needing external verification. These are capability assessments, not verified Ideal State claims.

Current evidence gives us useful foundations: topical ownership and competitor research, article and refresh workflows, publication gates, search reporting, discovery tools and affiliate-link infrastructure. It does not yet establish an autonomous, financially sustainable business or measured reader success.

The first learning steps are to establish actual owner effort and service outcomes, verify uncertain external setups, and test the new-article route against current writing guidance. The maintained registry and exception handling should make gaps observable. Reader email, affiliate activation and commission-to-cash evidence close important unfinished business loops. How this artifact guides work

The Ideal State defines the outcomes. The core story owns the front door and where each piece of the site sits. The topical map owns reader problems and content scope. The meets hub plan owns meet data and sources. The shared backlog holds selected actions. Session memory holds facts that are not in the code. Work changes the system and returns dated evidence to this page.
Before starting a work item, record:
The primary criterion and any related ones.
The observed gap, with dated evidence and what remains unknown.
The smallest intervention or experiment likely to move that outcome.
What would show improvement, what would disprove the assumption, and the observation window.
The one-time and recurring effort for Rex, the AI and vendor cost, and the authority needed.
The stop or rollback condition, and the evidence to return when done.

Completion has two meanings. The change is implemented and checked; the intended outcome has been observed. A deployment can complete the first without establishing the second. An investigation can succeed by ruling out a feature.

Proposed working rule for session close-out: a backlog item written for SwimTrack names the criterion it serves. No automatic loading, queue trigger, dashboard refresh or execution permission was installed by creating this page. Existing approved priorities stand while they are connected to outcomes.
Evidence and revision rules
Every criterion has a stable ID, a claim, a way to check it, current evidence and a next gap.
Keep criterion approval separate from evidence status. A proposed criterion is not an owner decision; a green test is not proof of a parent's outcome.
Use not measured, partial evidence, supported within scope or contradicted. Record the sample, period and limits. Missing evidence is not a failed result.
Separate what is observed from what is desired. A workflow being green does not verify the claim it serves.
Retain failed checks and conflicting observations. Reopen a supported claim when new evidence contradicts it or its evidence expires.
Set thresholds before judging outcomes. Where Rex has not set a target, record the decision as open. Do not invent revenue, workload or quality targets.
Read-only checks may gather evidence under existing authority. A check that spends money, contacts people, changes accounts, scrapes a ruled-out source or publishes needs its standing authorization.

Refine this page when Rex's intent changes, when evidence challenges a belief, or when a work item produces a meaningful result. Keep the version history and the reason for each change. Most sessions should update evidence; few should change criteria; changes to the central promise are deliberate.

Known tensions to manage
"Covered" depends on the organiser's software, not on the parent's region. Coverage will look random from the parent's side until the site explains it.
The coach owns the meet. The site's promise must never compete with the coach or imply an entry the coach did not make.
More articles raise coverage and the approval load at once. Rex's dissatisfaction with the voice is the live editorial problem; volume does not fix it.
Free first is the direction, and the pass is the only revenue. A fair test of the pass needs the live schedule to work first.
Portugal only, with frozen assets: four retired languages and four other federations' standards pages still build. They are not a target and must not become one by accident.
The operator is at the pool too. Meet-day reliability has to come from the system, not from Rex watching a log.
A system can run unattended and still deliver nothing. Judge autonomy alongside parent outcomes and honesty.
Starting point and next learning steps

The foundations are real: a 27-article library in two languages with a readability gate, the Portuguese time standards and converter, the season pages and the saved plan, a working Navigator app with last season's meets, an account and payment service built to a written contract, a writing engine on cron, a topical map of 106 pages and a plan for every Portuguese meet source. What does not yet exist is the season itself: live meet coverage this year, a service a parent can sign in to, regional calendars, an email that sends, and any measure of what parents do.

The first learning steps are the ones a parent would notice: confirm the constraint and the Navigator's place; make the live pages honest; get the Navigator live for a rehearsal meet before 24 October; build the door; and start counting saved seasons and returning parents. Listing them here starts none of them.
